AGIBOT G2 completes an initial chip-test line integration trial at JCET

The robot handles trays and separates tested output at an automotive-electronics plant; sustained production metrics remain undisclosed.

RobotsBeat ↗24 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A trial with a different customer

November 23 reporting describes an initial AGIBOT G2 production-line integration trial at JCET’s automotive-electronics facility in Shanghai’s Lingang area. This concerns a chip-handling process at a new customer, separate from the previously reported G2 deployment on Lens Technology smartphone test lines.

Handling around test equipment

The wheeled, dual-arm robot loads untested trays, removes tested trays and directs passing and failing output to designated channels. That sequence requires manipulation to coordinate with test equipment. It does not mean the robot independently performs the chips’ electrical tests.

Evidence remains trial-level

The partners plan further validation and process expansion. Published information does not provide a robot count, hourly throughput, sustained operating duration or human-intervention rate. These omissions prevent a reliable assessment of full-line economics from the integration trial alone.
